system_overview.purpose: Loan origination calculator for loan officers to price and submit loan applications

findings.description: No machine-readable API exists. The application only serves HTML via Struts JSP forwards. An AI agent cannot programmatically invoke loan calculations or submissions.
No API documentation, schema, or contract (OpenAPI, WSDL, etc.) exists.
No versioning strategy for any interface. The single /loan action path has no version prefix or content negotiation.

No application-level authentication. Identity relies entirely on container-managed auth (WebLogic) with request.getRemoteUser(). There is no mechanism for service-to-service authentication, API keys, OAuth tokens, or any credential an agent could present.
Hardcoded database credentials in source code (loan_app / loanApp2010). This is a critical security vulnerability and indicates no secrets management infrastructure.
No authorization model beyond container login. No role-based access control, no permission scoping, no ability to restrict agent actions to a subset of operations.

No idempotency controls on the loan submission operation. Repeated submit actions create duplicate database records. An AI agent retrying a failed/timed-out request would create duplicate loan applications with financial impact.
No transaction IDs, correlation IDs, or request deduplication mechanisms. The system provides no way for a caller to detect or prevent duplicate submissions.
Struts ActionForm uses request scope, so no server-side session state accumulates. Each request is self-contained.

No approval workflow or confirmation step exists at the system level. The submit action immediately writes to the database. There is no mechanism to require human review before a loan application is committed.

The two-step UI flow (calculate then submit) provides a rudimentary human checkpoint in the browser, but this is a UI concern only — there is no server-side enforcement that a human reviewed the quote before submission.
No logging framework is used. The application imports no logging library and produces no structured logs. Agent-initiated actions would be completely invisible.
No metrics, health checks, tracing, or audit trail. There is no way to monitor agent behavior, detect anomalies, or attribute actions to specific callers.

security_findings.description: SQL injection vulnerability in saveApplication() — applicant name is concatenated directly into SQL. An agent passing unvalidated input could corrupt or exfiltrate database contents.
Framework (Struts 1.3) has known unpatched CVEs with no available fixes.

recommendations: Modernize the application before considering agentic integration. The EOL technology stack makes incremental improvements impractical.
Rewrite or wrap with an API layer — expose loan calculation and submission as RESTful endpoints with JSON payloads and OpenAPI documentation.
Implement OAuth 2.0 or equivalent for machine-to-machine authentication with scoped permissions.
Add idempotency keys to all mutating operations (loan submission).
Introduce an approval queue — loan submissions should enter a pending review state rather than immediately committing.
Deploy structured logging and tracing from day one of any modernization effort.
Fix SQL injection immediately, regardless of agentic readiness goals.

to_remediation_required: Expose a REST or gRPC API with structured request/response
Implement service authentication (OAuth 2.0 / API keys minimum)
Add idempotency keys to the submission endpoint
Introduce structured logging with caller attribution
Migrate off EOL framework (Struts 1.3) and runtime (Java 5)
to_pilot_ready: Role-based access control with agent-specific scopes
Approval workflow / confirmation queue for loan submissions
